text: An IP firewall rule trusts a header claiming to be from a certain address. A VNet service endpoint trusts something stronger — Azure's own confirmation that traffic came from a specific subnet in a specific VNet.

An IP-based rule lets in anything claiming to be from a range. A VNet service endpoint rule lets in only traffic Azure itself confirms came from a specific subnet — network identity, not a spoofable header.

Enabling a service endpoint takes two matching configurations — the Microsoft.Sql endpoint on the subnet, and a Virtual Network rule on the Azure SQL server naming that exact subnet. Miss either side and it silently doesn't work.

A service endpoint still routes to Azure SQL's public endpoint, just through a tighter gate — it doesn't give the database a private IP. Next up: Private Endpoints and Private Link, which remove that public endpoint entirely.
